body_extras.body: Not for this PR, but the rest of the Firecrawl page has drifted from the spec: `formats` and `ignoreQueryParameters` aren't inputs, the `crawl` limit defaults to 20 rather than 100, and `crawlAndWait` isn't documented. I can open a follow-up for those.

reviews.head: ceb63ec22938bc199b1cac9490a70773924ede01
reviews.body: Docs LGTM overall, with a few wording suggestions.

comments.why: Marker policy. No docsUrl and the PR doesn't touch the contract test, so the heads-up applies. Keeps the author's note wording.
comments.expect: Actions marked _(not yet available)_ are not exposed to agents.
comments.body:
"Not yet available" doesn't tell readers what they can do with these actions today. They already work through the API, so I'd rather say that with `_(API only)_`. Your note already explains it, so only the marker changes:

```suggestion
This connector is currently available in **Agent Builder** only. Workflow support is planned for a future release. Actions marked _(API only)_ are not exposed to agents. Until workflow support is added, you can only run them through the [Run a connector](https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/kibana/operation/operation-post-actions-connector-id-execute) API.
```

Heads-up: `connector_spec_quality_contract.test.ts` checks these lines for the old `_(not yet available)_` text, so it needs a matching change there.


comments.why: "Becomes usable when workflow support is added" contradicts the note: the executor never checks isTool. Multi-statement input runs as one implicit transaction (agent description says so). Rollback wording unverified, so it asks.
comments.expect: becomes usable when workflow support is added
comments.body:
"Becomes usable when workflow support is added" reads as if it can't run today, but it already runs through the API. I'd also mention the single transaction, since it changes what happens when one statement fails. Could you confirm that part?

```suggestion
:   Run any SQL against the database. This action has no restrictions. You can run `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `DROP`, `COPY`, and data definition language (DDL) statements, and you can send several statements at once. They run in a single transaction, so if one fails, none of them apply. Use it only when you explicitly need a write or destructive operation. One result is returned per statement, with at most the first 1,000 rows of each. Agents can't use this action. Prefer **Query** for read-only access.
```

comments.why: searchRows runs SELECT *, so column-level grants fail. The bot's code thread was resolved by updating the agent description only, not the docs.
comments.expect: Search rows in a table by matching
comments.body:
I'd mention the permission this one needs, since **List Tables** also shows tables where the role can read only some columns:

```suggestion
:   Search rows in a table by matching a search term against one or more columns, using a case-insensitive partial match. Non-text columns are compared on their text representation. The role needs `SELECT` on every column of the table.
```

"Not yet available" doesn't tell readers what they can do with these actions today. They already work through the API, so I'd rather say that with `_(API only)_`. Your note already explains it, so only the marker changes:

comments.why: Global STS tokens are valid only in Regions enabled by default (AWS IAM docs). GovCloud and China ARNs pass the schema but can't use commercial STS. Bot raised the code side on aws_iam_role.ts:115. This asks only for the docs side.
comments.body: Could you confirm where IAM Role works while STS stays on the global endpoint (the bot raised it on `aws_iam_role.ts`)? From the AWS docs, tokens from the global endpoint only work in Regions enabled by default, and GovCloud and China roles can't use it. If that's how it ships, I'd add a short note here so readers in those Regions pick **AWS Credentials** instead.

comments.why: Em dashes, plus IAM Role still stores a long-lived IAM user key in Kibana to call AssumeRole.
comments.body:
Without the em dashes. I'd also say that IAM Role still needs a long-lived key to call STS, so readers who pick it for security reasons know what Kibana still stores:

```suggestion
    - **AWS Credentials**: authenticate with a long-lived IAM user access key and secret. Use this for simple setups where a dedicated IAM user is acceptable.
    - **AWS IAM Role**: authenticate by assuming an IAM role through AWS STS. The connector still uses an IAM user access key to call STS, then signs DynamoDB requests with short-lived role credentials. Use this for cross-account access or when your security policy requires role-based access.
```
